decisions.issues: Minor only: the seated chiefs carry no sandal-paste or ash forehead marks (2.1 asks for these, including on the heavy older chief, here at far right), and Padmini is walking with her stick rather than seated among them. Otherwise clean. The two balloons can sit on the low-detail laterite wall and ceiling at upper centre-right, clear of all faces.

Only one candidate listed. v02 matches the beat: the boy is grinning, sweat runs down his face, and his musket is grounded with both hands folded over the muzzle. His look (bare-chested, white mundu with red border, powder horn on a strap) matches the youth in 3.2/3.3, and the firing line behind is side-on in white mundus, consistent with 3.4. The open blue sky in the upper right gives clear space for the short recruit balloon and the medium caption without covering faces or hands.

Minor only. Ibrahim's ear-to-jaw scar is on the correct (anatomical left) side but reads slightly reddish rather than pale. Nagoji's inner-left-forearm scar is hidden by his crossed arms. Lettering space: the roof rafters at upper centre for Ibrahim and the plain wall at upper right for Padmini.

v02 (the only listed candidate) fails in four ways. (1) Nagoji has a curved ivory-hilted knife tucked into his mundu waistband, copied from his sheet; the chapter bible and prompt say no knife. (2) Revathi shows no grey threading in her hair and no clear sandalwood line at the hairline, unlike neighbouring panels 4.2 and 4.5. (3) The bastion is drawn as a large hilltop fort with a square tower over the roofline, outside the gate opening. The script asks for the small, grey, angled point of the new bastion seen far off through the open south gate. (4) Minor: the tall square tower reads as an older fort, not a new angled bastion. Otherwise the staging works: Revathi standing and gazing toward the gate, the steward walking away with palm-leaf bundles, the sunlit courtyard, the low table with palm leaves and a brass measure, and clear sky at upper right.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: a wide, sunlit Velinadu courtyard, Nagoji standing at left under the carved verandah, Revathi standing beside the low table of palm-leaf bundles and the brass grain measure with her gaze turned past Nagoji toward the open courtyard gate, the old steward walking away carrying a bundle of leaves, and clear open sky in the upper part of the frame for one balloon. Fix these points: Nagoji wears NO knife, dagger or hilt of any kind; his white mundu waistband is plain cloth with nothing tucked into it, and he has bare arms, the shoulder cloth and the silver chain of office only. Revathi must show visible first grey threading at her temple and through the front of her black braid, and a thin pale sandalwood line at her hairline, matching the neighbouring courtyard panels. The bastion must be seen THROUGH the open gate, framed between the two gate leaves: far off, small and grey above the palm tops, it is a single low, angled, pointed arrowhead bastion of a coastal fort wall. It is not a hilltop castle, not a tall square tower, and nothing of it rises above the house roofline elsewhere in the frame.

decisions.issues: Acceptable and fixes every r1 failure. Varma has black hair in a knot on his left side, the namam and pearl earrings from his sheet, and gold necklaces. Acceptable and fixes the r1 maker's label. The only candidate (v02) now shows the beat correctly: Varma has his right hand flat on the white coat. It has NO gold embroidery, gold border, kasavu stripe or gold piping on any edge, cuff or hem. The red waistcoat lies beside it. That means Varma's V13 face and fierce downward look; his black hair in the side knot above his LEFT ear; the namam mark and pearl earrings; his gold necklaces; the white bandage over his left shoulder; his bare chest and cream mundu with gold border. v02 is the only listed candidate, and it shows Nagoji DISMOUNTED, standing on the drill ground with his hands behind his back. It is a medium shot cropped at the thighs, with no horse anywhere. Behind him an active musket firing line with turbaned soldiers aiming at targets crowds what should be a quiet dawn lesson on a near-empty ground. He gazes upward into the distance instead of level toward the off-panel Prince. Face, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temples, costume and the sun behind him are all correct.
decisions.correction: Nagoji is still MOUNTED on Kayal, exactly as in the panels before and after, so frame a tight head-and-shoulders close-up from mid-chest up with the camera level with his eyes, not looking up at him; no legs, boots or ground beneath him show. At most the top of Kayal's black mane and the tips of her bay ears appear along the bottom edge in front of him. He is turned three-quarter toward frame RIGHT, looking level and steady at the Prince, who is off panel to the right and is not drawn. His hands are out of frame. The low golden early-morning sun sits directly behind his head and shoulders as a warm rim light, against a soft gold sky with the dim laterite bastion behind. The drill ground behind him is quiet and nearly empty: no firing line, no musketeers, no soldiers aiming, no other figures in the foreground. Keep what worked: his face, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw, grey at the temples, Kerala topknot, tiny flush gold ear stud, white coat with plain brass buttons, red waistcoat and the silver chain of office over the coat. Leave the upper third and the open sky to the right of his head plain and low-detail for three speech balloons.

Clean.
